title: Complete Guide to CCPA & California Privacy Rights
metaDescription: Master CCPA compliance with our comprehensive guide. Learn your California privacy rights, CPRA updates, and actionable steps to protect your data.
intro: The California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA) grants California residents powerful rights over their personal data. This guide explains your privacy rights, how to exercise them, and steps businesses must take for compliance.
prerequisites: Access to email for making requests

steps.title: Understand Your CCPA Rights
steps.description: The CCPA grants California consumers five fundamental privacy rights regarding their personal information collected by businesses.
actions: Right to Know: Request what personal information is collected, used, shared, or sold
Right to Delete: Request deletion of your personal information
Right to Opt-Out: Stop the sale or sharing of your personal information
Right to Correct: Request correction of inaccurate personal information
Right to Non-Discrimination: Not be treated differently for exercising your rights
steps.proTip: The CPRA (California Privacy Rights Act) expanded these rights in 2023, adding the right to correct information and limit use of sensitive personal information.
steps.warning: Rights only apply to businesses that meet CCPA thresholds: $25M+ annual revenue, buy/sell 100k+ consumers' data, or derive 50%+ revenue from selling personal information.

steps.title: Identify What Information is Protected
steps.description: CCPA protects a broad range of personal information beyond just names and addresses. Understanding what's covered helps you make informed requests.
actions: Review identifiers: name, address, email, phone, Social Security number, driver's license
Check commercial information: purchase history, preferences, tendencies
Examine internet activity: browsing history, search history, interaction with websites
Consider biometric data: fingerprints, voiceprints, facial recognition data
Note geolocation data: precise location information from devices
Understand sensitive personal information: race, religion, health data, sexual orientation
steps.proTip: Use privacy-focused tools like Incognito Browser to limit data collection while browsing and reduce the amount of information companies can gather about you.

steps.title: Exercise Your Right to Know
steps.description: Request information about what personal data companies have collected about you, how they use it, and who they share it with.
actions: Visit the company's privacy policy page to find their 'Do Not Sell My Personal Information' link
Look for 'Your Privacy Choices' or 'Privacy Rights' sections on websites
Submit a request through the company's designated method (web form, email, phone)
Provide required verification information (usually name, email, phone number)
Wait for the company's response within 45 days (extendable to 90 days)
Review the information provided and follow up if incomplete
steps.proTip: Companies must provide information in a portable format. Request data in commonly used formats like CSV or PDF for easier review.

steps.title: Opt Out of Data Sales and Sharing
steps.description: Stop companies from selling or sharing your personal information with third parties for cross-context behavioral advertising.
actions: Look for 'Do Not Sell or Share My Personal Information' links on websites
Click the link and follow the opt-out process (usually a simple form)
Install browser extensions that automatically submit opt-out requests
Use the Global Privacy Control (GPC) signal in privacy-focused browsers
Submit requests to data brokers that may have your information
Set up calendar reminders to renew opt-out requests annually
steps.proTip: Enable Global Privacy Control in Incognito Browser to automatically signal your opt-out preference to websites that support this standard.
steps.warning: Opt-out requests may need to be renewed periodically, and some companies have different processes for different types of data sharing.

steps.title: Request Deletion of Your Data
steps.description: Ask companies to delete the personal information they have collected about you, subject to certain exceptions for business operations.
actions: Identify companies you want to request deletion from
Use the company's designated deletion request method
Verify your identity as required by the company
Understand exceptions: companies can keep data for legal compliance, security, or completing transactions
Follow up if you don't receive confirmation within 45 days
Keep records of your deletion requests and company responses
steps.warning: Companies may retain some data for legitimate business purposes like completing transactions, detecting fraud, or complying with legal obligations.

steps.title: Understand Business Compliance Requirements
steps.description: If you're a business owner, ensure your company meets CCPA compliance requirements to avoid penalties and protect customer rights.
actions: Determine if your business meets CCPA thresholds for compliance
Update your privacy policy to include CCPA-required disclosures
Implement processes to handle consumer rights requests within required timeframes
Train staff on CCPA requirements and consumer rights
Establish data mapping to understand what personal information you collect
Set up systems to verify consumer identities for rights requests
Create 'Do Not Sell or Share' links and opt-out mechanisms
steps.proTip: Consider conducting a privacy impact assessment to identify compliance gaps and prioritize improvements.
steps.warning: CCPA violations can result in fines up to $7,500 per violation. California's Privacy Protection Agency actively enforces these requirements.

faqs.question: Who does the CCPA apply to?
faqs.answer: CCPA applies to businesses that collect California residents' personal information and meet at least one threshold: $25M+ annual revenue, buy/sell/share personal information of 100k+ consumers, or derive 50%+ revenue from selling personal information.

faqs.question: What's the difference between CCPA and CPRA?
faqs.answer: CPRA (California Privacy Rights Act) is an amendment that expanded CCPA starting in 2023. It added new rights like correcting inaccurate information, limiting sensitive data use, and created the California Privacy Protection Agency for enforcement.

faqs.question: How long do companies have to respond to my requests?
faqs.answer: Companies must acknowledge your request within 10 days and provide a response within 45 days. They can extend this to 90 days for complex requests but must notify you of the extension and reason.

faqs.question: Can companies charge me for exercising my privacy rights?
faqs.answer: No, companies cannot charge fees for processing your CCPA rights requests. However, they may charge reasonable fees for excessive or repetitive requests, particularly for deletion requests.

faqs.question: Do I need to be a California resident to have CCPA rights?
faqs.answer: Yes, CCPA rights are specifically for California residents. However, some companies extend similar privacy rights to all users regardless of location for operational simplicity.

faqs.question: What happens if a company doesn't respond to my request?
faqs.answer: You can file a complaint with the California Privacy Protection Agency. For data breaches involving unencrypted personal information, you may also have the right to sue for damages of $100-$750 per incident.

faqs.question: How do I know if my personal information was sold?
faqs.answer: Use your Right to Know to request information about data sales. Companies must disclose the categories of personal information sold and the categories of third parties who received it in the past 12 months.

faqs.question: Can I authorize someone else to make privacy requests on my behalf?
faqs.answer: Yes, you can authorize an agent to make requests for you. You'll need to provide written permission to the agent and verify your identity with the business, unless you give the agent power of attorney.
